authors: Kris Otteman, Linda Fielder, Emily Lewis
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association (JAVMA)

mcqs.q: How does this commentary frame the identification and reporting of animal cruelty for veterinarians?
o: A core professional and ethical imperative
Solely the responsibility of law enforcement
A task limited to forensic specialists
mcqs.e: The piece positions recognizing and reporting cruelty as a professional/ethical duty for veterinarians.

mcqs.q: Whom does the commentary call on to prepare graduates to confidently recognize and report cruelty?
mcqs.e: It calls on veterinary educators to train graduates to identify, document, and report suspected cruelty.

authors: Lena DeTar, Jaclyn Bubnell, M Erin Henry, Daniel Lopez, Jessica Reed
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association (JAVMA)

mcqs.q: What change in euthanasia from the target community was associated with the targeted TNVR project?
mcqs.e: The study reported a roughly 3-fold reduction in euthanasia from the target community (OR 3.89, 95% CI 1.55-9.8).

mcqs.q: Where did the project produce its largest impact?
mcqs.e: The largest impact was in the community, with residents reporting improved cat welfare, fewer births, and renewed trust in the SPCA.

mcqs.q: What effect did the service-learning model have on participating veterinary students?
o: Increased on-site surgical volume and confidence
Decreased their interest in shelter work
mcqs.e: Students increased surgical volume by about 3 procedures and reported gains in confidence and perceived readiness.

authors: Lena G DeTar, Savannah M Martin
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association (JAVMA)

mcqs.q: In what investigative context is the microwave radiation injury in this kitten most relevant?
mcqs.e: Listed keywords (forensics, maltreatment, microwave radiation, burn management) tie the case to non-accidental injury investigation.

mcqs.q: Which clinical skill does the case emphasize for shelter and forensic veterinarians?
o: Recognizing and documenting distinctive thermal burn patterns
mcqs.e: The report highlights recognizing, documenting, and managing the distinctive burn pattern of microwave radiation injury.

authors: Bruce G Kornreich, Diego G Diel, Lena G Detar, Elisha A Frye, Laura B Goodman, Gary R Whittaker

mcqs.q: What approximate mortality does H5N1 avian influenza cause in cats per this initiative?
mcqs.e: H5N1 causes severe disease in cats with mortality up to roughly 70%.

mcqs.q: What setting is central to the consortium's pilot feline H5N1 surveillance?
mcqs.e: The pilot tests cats at shelters, clinics, and veterinary hospitals in New York state.

mcqs.q: Which question about feline H5N1 does the consortium aim to answer?
o: Whether feline-to-feline transmission and community prevalence occur
Best surgical approach for infected cats
mcqs.e: Little is known about feline-to-feline transmission, vector potential, or community-cat infection prevalence, which the consortium targets.

authors: Amanda Garrick, A Russell Moore, Nida Chornarm, Jennifer Hawley, Nicole Dixon, Michael R Lappin

mcqs.q: What happened to canine CRP values after 14 weeks of storage at -80 degrees C?
o: They increased by an average of about 3.58 mg/L
mcqs.e: CRP did not falsely drop with freeze-thaw; values increased by an average of 3.58 mg/L after 14 weeks at -80 C.

mcqs.q: What does the study conclude about using different commercial CRP assays for serial monitoring?
o: Any assay can be interchanged freely
The same assay should be used consistently
Assay choice does not affect results
mcqs.e: The three assays were not analytically equivalent, so the same assay should be used for monitoring.

mcqs.q: How did CRP behave with H3N2 influenza infection in dogs?
o: CRP rose with clinical signs of infection
mcqs.e: Dogs with clinical signs of H3N2 infection had increases in CRP, supporting its use as an inflammatory marker.

authors: Petra Černá, Evan Ross, Lance Visser, Riley Ellis-Reis, McKenna Willis, Jennifer Hawley, Michael R Lappin

mcqs.q: What cardiac findings were documented in cats with feline infectious peritonitis?
o: LV wall thickening and elevated cardiac troponin I
mcqs.e: 55% had thickened LV walls and many had elevated cTnI, findings suggestive of myocarditis/myocardial injury.

mcqs.q: What happened to elevated cardiac troponin I after 12 weeks of antiviral treatment?
o: It normalized to <0.20 ng/mL in all 6 cats retested
mcqs.e: All 6 cats with initially increased cTnI had it normalize to <0.20 ng/mL after 12 weeks of antiviral therapy.

authors: Andrea V Scorza, Christian M Leutenegger, Cecilia Lozoya, Jeffrey Tereski, Samantha Loo, Pablo D Jimenez Castro, Michael R Lappin

mcqs.q: Which Giardia duodenalis assemblages are the zoonotic ones in this study?
mcqs.e: Assemblages A and B can be zoonotic, whereas C, D, F, and G are dog/cat-adapted and not human-infective.

mcqs.q: How did the beta-giardin qPCR compare to multilocus genotyping for detecting zoonotic assemblages?
o: It strongly agreed and is cheaper/faster
It only worked for non-zoonotic assemblages
mcqs.e: bg-qPCR agreed closely with multilocus genotyping (kappa 0.828) for A/B, offering a cheaper, faster option.

authors: Charles T Talbot, Melissa Brewer, McKenna Willis, Kris Kofron, Sarah B Shropshire, Kelly S Santangelo, Kristin M Zersen, Michael R Lappin
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association

mcqs.q: How did the in-house dot-blot ELISA for CPV antibody titers compare to reference HI assays?
mcqs.e: The dot-blot ELISA showed strong agreement (Spearman 0.72-0.92) and 96-97% sensitivity vs HI assays.

mcqs.q: What is the main clinical use of rapid CPV titer screening in blood-donor dogs?
o: Selecting high-titer plasma for passive immunotherapy of parvo patients
mcqs.e: Accurate titers help select high-titer plasma from donors for passive immunotherapy of critically ill parvo patients.

mcqs.q: What proportion of dogs with vaccination history had protective CPV titers?
mcqs.e: 93% of the 43 dogs with vaccination history had protective titers.

authors: Megan Slaughter, Chi-Hsuan Sung, Jan Suchodolski, Rachel Pilla, Camille Torres-Hendersen, Michael R Lappin
journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: What effect did probiotic Enterococcus lactis SF68 have on amoxicillin-clavulanate-induced changes in cats?
o: Normalized the feline dysbiosis index and increased secondary bile acids
mcqs.e: The probiotic group showed normalized feline DI and increased secondary bile acids by day 14 vs placebo.

mcqs.q: What practical recommendation follows from these findings?
o: Co-supplement SF68 when cats need amoxicillin-clavulanate
Use probiotics only after diarrhea resolves
mcqs.e: Findings support supplementing SF68 in cats with a clinical need for amoxicillin-clavulanate.

authors: Rachael Isdale, Jamie A E Myers, Susan Holzmer, Kaci Shaw, Vickie King, Jessica Y Rodriguez, Jennifer Hawley, Michael R Lappin

mcqs.q: What tick reduction did a single topical dose of selamectin plus sarolaner achieve in cats?
mcqs.e: Revolution Plus produced 100% reduction of I. scapularis ticks vs placebo.

mcqs.q: What was the effect on Borrelia burgdorferi transmission in treated cats?
o: No treated cat developed B. burgdorferi antibodies or skin DNA
Only antibody but not DNA was blocked
mcqs.e: None of the RP-treated cats developed B. burgdorferi antibodies or skin DNA, indicating blocked transmission.

authors: Kara M Maslyn, Jennifer R Hawley, Craig E Webb, Michael R Lappin

mcqs.q: What primary effect did telmisartan demonstrate in healthy dogs?
o: Antioxidative effects (upregulated SOD, total antioxidant capacity, glutathione peroxidase)
A marked rise in blood pressure
mcqs.e: Telmisartan significantly upregulated SOD, total antioxidant capacity, and glutathione peroxidase, showing antioxidative effects.

mcqs.q: What did the study find regarding blood pressure and cytokines in these healthy dogs?
o: No significant changes in blood pressure, CBC, or cytokines
mcqs.e: No significant changes in arterial blood pressure, CBC, or cytokines/chemokines were detected.

authors: Haley E Jost, Michala de Linde Henriksen, Jennifer Hawley, Michael R Lappin
journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: Could this pilot study confirm Leptospira as a cause of feline endogenous uveitis?
o: No, all aqueous humor samples were PCR-negative for Leptospira
Yes, via positive aqueous humor cultures
No, because no cats had any antibodies
mcqs.e: All aqueous humor samples were Leptospira PCR-negative, so causation could not be proven (only 2 cats had Pomona titers).

mcqs.q: Which infectious agent had the highest seropositivity among the uveitis cats?
mcqs.e: Serum antibodies to Bartonella species were common, found in 21/37 (56.8%) of uveitis cats.
